name: Motor-Driven Cycle
description: Alabama's light motorcycle class, which takes in mopeds and motor scooters: a motorcycle whose motor produces 5 brake horsepower (3,730 W) or less and that weighs under 200 lb fully equipped, plus any bicycle with a motor attached. An electric bicycle over the e-bike limits lands here. Defined by Code of Alabama §32-1-1.1(37), with the e-bike exclusion added by HB 99 (Act 2021-134).
restrictions: A motorcycle or motor scooter (a seat or saddle and no more than three wheels) whose motor produces no more than 5 brake horsepower (3,730 W) and that weighs less than 200 lb fully equipped
Any bicycle with a motor attached is a motor-driven cycle too; the statute sets no power limit for one
A bicycle whose motor is 750 W or more, or that fits none of the three e-bike classes, is no longer an electric bicycle and lands here
Alabama law has no separate moped category; the state treats a moped as a motor-driven cycle
Riders need Class M on their license; at 14 or 15 they can get a Class M restricted to motor-driven cycles (restriction B) by passing the motorcycle knowledge test or an MSF Basic Riders Course
Riders 17 and younger are held to the graduated license's operating hours and restrictions
Riders and passengers must wear a motorcycle helmet meeting Alabama's standard, and shoes
Registered and tagged to ride on public highways, and must carry liability insurance; exempt from title
Needs at least one working brake, which the state may inspect and disapprove
At night or in poor visibility, can't go faster than 35 mph unless its headlamp lights a person or vehicle 300 feet ahead
